Common questions

Why do websites reject my iPhone photos?

Since iOS 11, iPhones save photos in HEIC format because it takes about half the space of JPG. Many form and upload systems — job applications, visa forms, university portals, older websites — were built for JPG and PNG only, so they refuse HEIC files or fail silently. Converting to JPG fixes it.

Can I stop my iPhone from saving HEIC photos?

Yes, if you would rather shoot JPG directly:

  1. Open Settings on your iPhone
  2. Tap Camera, then Formats
  3. Choose Most Compatible

New photos will be saved as JPG. Photos already on your phone stay HEIC — convert those here.

Will the JPG look worse than the original?

At 92% quality the difference is not visible in normal use, and the file is still much smaller than a PNG. If a form has a strict size limit, lower the quality slider a little — 80% is fine for documents and ID photos.

JPG or PNG — which should I choose?

JPG for photos and forms: it is accepted everywhere and keeps file sizes small. PNG is lossless and better for screenshots or images with text, but the files are several times larger and some forms reject them for size.

Are my photos uploaded to a server?

No. The conversion runs entirely in your browser on this device — the files are never sent anywhere. You can even load this page, turn on airplane mode, and it still works.
